title: Reusable spark-band component with ARIA summary and lazy aggregation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Several dashboards rely on bespoke sparkline and band components implemented inconsistently across products. This leads to duplicated logic, accessibility variance (different aria summaries), and performance regressions when many small charts render on the same page.

Goal: Design a single, reusable 'spark-band' primitive optimized for dense time-series displays. It should: (1) provide a concise ARIA summary for screen readers, (2) expose a small API for visual and interaction variants (line, area, band, micro-bar), (3) support lazy aggregation/decimation for high-point series, (4) adopt tokens for color/spacing, and (5) include a Canvas-first implementation with an accessible DOM fallback for legacy browsers/screen readers.
proposed_api: props: {dataSeries: number[], variant: 'line'|'area'|'band'|'micro', showLegendHint: boolean, summaryLabel: string, samplingStrategy: 'time-window'|'size-based'|'quantile', tokens: string (optional theme override), interactive: boolean, onFocusSummaryRequest: (id)=>void}
token_guidelines: Use chart-color-foreground for lines, chart-color-band for filled ranges, chart-contrast-low for grid strokes. Respect spacing-token-xxs for padding around micro charts. Prefer CSS variables (token: --rw-chart-*) and document fallbacks for older embed contexts.
accessibility_requirements: 1) Each spark-band must expose a succinct aria-label summarizing metric, time-span, and critical anomalies for the last N points. 2) Provide keyboard focusable container with an optional expanded 'summary on demand' panel (aria-controls). 3) Ensure reduced-motion preference stops animated transitions. 4) Ensure color contrast of band edge > 3:1 for small glyphs and 4.5:1 for key interactive markers. 5) Add role=img and aria-describedby link to a live region that updates when keyboard focus moves between series variants.
performance_plan: Canvas-first rendering with Layered compositing: draw static grid and bands to an offscreen canvas and reuse; dynamic token-based coloring via small per-series overlay canvas. Implement size-based decimation by default for series > 300 points and time-window aggregation for streaming series. Use requestIdleCallback to precompute quantile aggregation for background renders and requestAnimationFrame for visible updates. Provide feature flag to enable GPU compositing for supported browsers. Add perf marks around render loop and expose perf metric events to Console tracing endpoint: charts.render.start / charts.render.end.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision (2026-02-25): Canvas-first offers best density and layering performance; SVG reserved for interactive expanded views and accessibility fallbacks.
Trade-off: Canvas reduces DOM semantics so we must surface semantic summaries via dedicated ARIA regions rather than relying on DOM nodes for each point.
Decision (2026-03-01): Default samplingStrategy = 'size-based' to prioritize consistent visual density across viewports; allow overrides for analytics consumers wanting exact points.
Trade-off: Using CSS tokens increases theming consistency but requires documented escape hatches for third-party embedded apps that cannot consume our token set.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec and Figma components created and annotated with token mapping.
Accessible ARIA summary pattern documented with examples for multi-series and single-series cases.
Prototype implemented in Storybook with three variants (line, band, micro) and automated visual snapshots.
Performance benchmark: page with 200 micro-sparks (each 500 points) renders initial paint < 800ms on target mid-tier machine and interactive < 1200ms.
Engineering PR with Canvas-first implementation merged and feature-flag gated; design review approved in PR comments.
QA test plan with keyboard navigation, voiceover narration checks, and contrast verification added to test matrix.
engineering_notes: Front-end owners: use OffscreenCanvas where available; fallback to standard canvas with offscreen buffer for older Chromium/Firefox. Expose a lightweight sample API so infra can attach KV-caching of computed aggregates for repeated mounts. Add ability to opt-in to prefix caching of last-view aggregates to reduce recompute on rerenders.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Initial ticket created after cross-team sync; prototype brief sketched in Figma.
2026-02-25: Decided on Canvas-first strategy after engineering perf spike tests; added ARIA live region pattern to requirements.
2026-03-02: Prototype Storybook demo (line + band) posted at https://storybook.redwood.dev/?path=/story/spark-band--basic; shared with PM and Accessibility for feedback.
2026-03-08: Accessibility review: adjust ARIA summary to include last-seen timestamp and anomaly flag; reduced motion behavior clarified.
2026-03-12: Engineering spike completed for lazy aggregation; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web-ui/pull/4723
qa_and_usability: Test matrix: keyboard focus order, summary panel open/close, screen reader narration (NVDA/VoiceOver), contrast checks, reduced-motion simulation, high-density page stress test (200 sparks). Schedule 1-hour usability session with two power users and capture qualitative notes.
next_steps: 1) Finalize Figma tokens and publish design tokens package. 2) Engineering to merge spike PR behind flag and add perf telemetry. 3) Run synthetic load test in Console sandbox and validate SLO. 4) Prepare migration guide for legacy spark components. 5) Schedule handoff demo with platform FE team.
